where: Section 2, Deutsch bullet (and repeated in Quiz Q4 answer)
problem: "He also gave the first algorithm with a proven quantum speedup" overstates the 1985 paper. The 1985 algorithm succeeds only with probability 1/2 and does not by itself give a proven separation from classical algorithms; the standard first proven (deterministic, single-query) separation is the Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm of 1992.
fix: "He also gave the first quantum algorithm for a black-box problem, showing one query can beat any classical algorithm; the clean, deterministic version of this separation came with Deutsch and Jozsa in 1992."

problem: The cell text "one result, probability |amplitude|²" contains pipe characters, which are the table's column separators, so the row will break into extra columns and display wrongly.
fix: Write it without pipes, for example "one result, with probability equal to the squared magnitude of its amplitude".

where: Figure (gantt spec and its aria text)
problem: Bars of several years' length are drawn for one-year results (Deutsch 1985–1994, BB84 1984–1994, Grover 1996–2000). A reader takes the bar ends as the years when the work happened, so Grover appears to run until 2000 and Deutsch until 1994.
fix: Use point or short markers at the actual years (Feynman 1982, BB84 1984, Deutsch 1985, Shor 1994, Grover 1996) and let the aria text name those single years.

problem: "Unitary gates are reversible, so a quantum circuit has no built-in erasure" can mislead: measurement and reset do discard information, and ancilla qubits are uncomputed and thrown away. Only the gate itself is information-preserving.
fix: "Every unitary gate is reversible, so the gate alone never discards information; erasure in a quantum circuit happens only through measurement or reset, not inside the gates."

where: Section 3, end of the paragraph after the table
problem: "The last row of the table is the honest summary" has no clear referent; the last row lists extra resources, and the sentence that follows talks about speed, not resources.
fix: "The extra-resource row is the honest summary: quantum computing is not a faster processor for the same programs; interference and entanglement are a different resource that only some problems can spend."
